title: Slashy vs Avec: AI Email Client Comparison for Series A-D in 2026
summary: Explore Slashy vs Avec AI email client comparison for Series A-D startups. Understand features, pricing, and use cases in 2026 to make the best choice.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


Avec is a free iPhone email app for Gmail that shows your important emails one at a time, lets you swipe through them, and drafts replies from your voice notes. Slashy is a paid AI-native email and calendar client with memory-based drafting, CRM integration, open tracking, follow-up reminders and auto-labeling on one $300 per year plan. Pick Avec for a fast free phone inbox; pick Slashy if you run a team's deal flow and calendar out of email.


When choosing an AI email client, the architectural choice matters more than the feature list. Slashy was built AI-first from day one. The memory system learns continuously from emails you send, receive, and respond to, with draft acceptance climbing from around 30% on day 1 to 80%+ by day 30. Avec took a different path: a focused iPhone app that turns the inbox into a stack you swipe through. Both are full email apps that replace the default one, but they solve different problems. Slashy is an email and calendar client with memory-adapted personalization, open tracking, and unified inbox across multiple accounts. Avec optimizes for getting through a Gmail inbox on your phone in as little time as possible.


## What are the key AI-native features of Slashy and Avec?


Slashy's in-house proprietary memory system learns your writing style, tone, recipients, response timing, and scheduling preferences continuously. A specialized memory agent adapts and organizes those memories based on emails you send, receive, and respond to. AI-draft acceptance rates climb from around 30% on day 1 to over 80% by day 30 as the system refines its understanding. Slashy ships with AI drafts in your writing tone, an inline AI Assistant inside the composer, auto-labeling across seven categories (Important / Calendar / Billing / Newsletter / Order / Other / Work), follow-up reminders with ghost detection, and a calendar sidebar that lives next to your inbox. The Professional tier at $300/year includes CRM integration, open tracking with device and count, and iMessage for drafting replies and triaging urgent emails.


Avec is an iPhone email app that works with your existing Gmail account ([avec.ai](https://www.avec.ai/) , read October 27, 2026). It "prioritizes your inbox and shows your important emails one by one", and you swipe to mark each one done or save it for later. You can speak a few key points and Avec drafts the email, and its site says those drafts "sound distinctively like you." Smart notifications summarize what a new message is about and what to do next. A memory system, calendar, open tracking and CRM integration are not documented on its site.


The core difference is scope. Slashy runs email, calendar and follow-ups on every device. Avec is built to make a phone inbox fast.


## How do Slashy and Avec compare in user experience?


Slashy provides a complete email and calendar client with AI integrated into every surface. Avec is a lightweight iPhone app built around one email at a time.


Slashy's onboarding begins with signing in to Gmail, Google Workspace, Outlook.com, or Microsoft 365, then the memory system starts learning immediately from your inbox history. The calendar sidebar appears next to your email list, and the command palette (Cmd+K) surfaces drafting, scheduling, and triage functions in one interface. Open tracking, follow-up reminders with ghost detection, and auto-labeling work without configuration. The Mac desktop app and iOS app provide the same feature set across devices.


Avec replaces the Gmail app on your phone. The experience centers on a stack of important emails, one-swipe handling for the rest, voice-to-draft replies, and notifications with summaries. Its site offers an iOS download and lists no desktop or web app.


The friction point is different. Slashy asks your whole team to switch clients on desktop and phone. Avec asks one person to switch the email app on their iPhone. If you want AI across email, calendar, and memory in one product, Slashy delivers that. If you mostly read and answer Gmail on your phone and want it to feel lighter, Avec fits.


## What use cases are best suited for Slashy versus Avec?


Slashy excels when email and calendar need to work as one product. Founders sending 200 emails a day, operations leads coordinating across time zones, and sales teams managing deal velocity benefit from Slashy's calendar sidebar next to the inbox, AI drafts that adapt to recipient context, and follow-up reminders with ghost detection. The memory system learns scheduling preferences alongside writing style, so meeting-heavy roles get smarter availability suggestions over time. CRM integration on the Professional tier ($300/year) makes Slashy the stronger pick for teams that need deal context inside the inbox: Attio and HubSpot.


> "After launch, email exploded. 10+ meetings daily, 50 unread by end of day. Slashy's how I make sense of it all."
>
>
> Sid, Founder of Clodo


Avec fits individuals who handle most of their Gmail on an iPhone and want to clear it fast. Its stack and swipe model is the honest strength here: it makes a long inbox feel short. Calendar and CRM features are not documented.


The deciding factor is scope. Slashy is a full client with memory, calendar, and triage across devices. Avec is a fast, free phone inbox.


An inbox that understands the next step


Slashy uses the context in your email and calendar to draft, schedule, remember, and follow through.

**Choose Slashy Professional ($30/user/month month-to-month, $300/year annual) if:**

**Choose Avec if:**


- You handle most of your Gmail on an iPhone and want a free app that shows important mail first.
- You do not need calendar, CRM or desktop features in your email app.


## How do the pricing structures of Slashy and Avec differ?


Slashy Professional costs $30/user/month month-to-month, or $300/year billed annually, with a 7-day free trial and custom pricing for Enterprise. Avec is "available for free on the App Store" ([avec.ai](https://www.avec.ai/) , read October 27, 2026); its site lists no paid plan.


Slashy's pricing reflects the scope of what ships on the Professional tier: AI drafts with continuous memory learning, calendar sidebar, CRM integration, open tracking with device and count, follow-up reminders with ghost detection, auto-labeling across seven categories, iMessage triage, and unified inbox across multiple accounts. The memory system's acceptance ramp (around 30% on day 1 to 80%+ by day 30) delivers compounding value the longer you use it.


Avec is a phone-first app for one person's Gmail rather than a team email and calendar client, so free is a fair price for what it covers and a real advantage if you only need that.


Tier Annual price What you get

**Avec** Free on the App Store iPhone Gmail app: priority stack, swipe triage, voice drafting, summary notifications


The budget question is scope. Slashy replaces your email and calendar client on every device. Avec replaces the email app on your iPhone.


## What customer support options are available with Slashy and Avec?


Slashy provides customer support tailored for teams moving to an AI-native email and calendar client, but specific support-channel details (email, chat, response SLAs) are not published on slashy.com. The 7-day free trial on the Professional tier ($300/year) gives new users hands-on access before committing, and the product ships with onboarding that starts the memory system learning immediately. Enterprise customers receive custom support agreements as part of their contract.


Avec listshi@avec.ai as its contact address; support channels and response times are not documented on its site.


For Slashy, the product's inline AI Assistant and command palette (Cmd+K) reduce support dependency by surfacing drafting, scheduling, and triage functions directly in the interface. The memory system's continuous learning means fewer manual configurations over time.


If support-channel specifics matter to your evaluation, verify both products' current support pages before deciding.


## What to choose if...


- You want an in-house memory system that learns your writing voice, tone, recipients, and scheduling preferences over time.
- You need CRM integration at the inbox tier (Attio and HubSpot ship with Professional).
- You want a calendar sidebar that lives next to your inbox, not a separate app.
- You need SOC 2 Type II and CASA Tier 2 compliance with data encrypted at rest and in transit.
- You want open tracking with ghost detection and follow-up reminders built into the inbox.


**Choose Avec if:**


- You want a free AI email app and only use Gmail.
- You read and answer most email on your iPhone and like clearing it one message at a time.
- You would rather dictate a reply than type it.


**Choose Gmail with Gemini if:**


- Free matters more than voice learning, CRM integration, or calendar-sidebar workflows.
- You are already deep in the Google Workspace ecosystem and prefer not to add another paid tool.
